title_en: Decision of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Article Numbers of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China Cited in Judicial Interpretations and Other Documents

articles.content_en: 1. Article 22 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Opinions on the People's Court's Adjudication of Loan Cases (Fa [Min] Fa [1991] No. 21) is adjusted as follows: "Where the person subject to enforcement may transfer, sell, or conceal the property subject to enforcement, the People's Court shall promptly take enforcement measures. If the person subject to enforcement resists enforcement and constitutes obstruction of civil action, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Articles 102 and 224 of the Civil Procedure Law."

2. Article 111 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where, after the People's Court has made an advance execution, according to a legally effective judgment, the applicant shall return the benefits obtained from the advance execution, the provisions of Article 210 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply."

3. Article 132 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where a party applies to the People's Court for a payment order in accordance with Article 191 of the Civil Procedure Law, an application fee of 100 yuan shall be paid per case. If the supervision procedure is terminated due to the debtor's objection, the application fee shall be borne by the applicant; if the debtor raises no objection, the application fee shall be borne by the debtor."

4. Article 134 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where a party applies to the People's Court for a public summons for exhortation in accordance with Article 195 of the Civil Procedure Law, an application fee of 100 yuan shall be paid per case. The application fee and the announcement fee shall be borne by the applicant."

5. Article 135 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where a party initiates a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with Articles 198 and 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the case acceptance fee shall be paid in accordance with Article 5(4) of the Measures for the Charging of Litigation Fees by the People's Courts."

6. Article 204 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where a party applies for retrial of a mediation statement that has already taken legal effect, the provisions of Article 184 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply, and the application shall be filed within two years after the mediation statement takes legal effect."

7. Article 212 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The two-year period referred to in Article 184 of the Civil Procedure Law is a fixed period, which shall be calculated from the day following the date on which the judgment or ruling takes legal effect."

8. Article 221 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where, in accordance with Article 194 of the Civil Procedure Law, the debtor raises a written objection within the statutory period, the People's Court shall not review whether the objection is well-founded and shall directly issue a ruling to terminate the supervision procedure. If the debtor does not object to the debt itself but merely claims lack of ability to pay, the validity of the payment order shall not be affected."

9. Article 222 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The written ruling rejecting an application for a payment order under Article 193 of the Civil Procedure Law and the written ruling terminating the supervision procedure under Article 194 of the Civil Procedure Law shall be signed by the judge and the clerk, and affixed with the seal of the People's Court."

10. Article 225 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The time limit for a creditor to apply to the People's Court for enforcement of a payment order shall be governed by Article 215 of the Civil Procedure Law."

11. Article 226 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The term 'holder of an instrument' as used in Article 195 of the Civil Procedure Law refers to the last holder of the instrument before it was stolen, lost, or destroyed."

13. Article 236 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where the People's Court notifies the payer to stop payment in accordance with Article 196 of the Civil Procedure Law, such notification shall comply with the provisions on property preservation. If the payer, after receiving the notice to stop payment, refuses to make payment, in addition to the compulsory measures that may be taken in accordance with Articles 102 and 103 of the Civil Procedure Law, the payer shall still bear the payment obligation after the judgment."

14. Article 237 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "After the People's Court terminates the procedure of public summons for exhortation in accordance with Article 198 of the Civil Procedure Law, if the applicant or the claimant initiates a lawsuit with the People's Court, the jurisdiction shall be determined in accordance with Article 27 of the Civil Procedure Law."

15. Article 238 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The written ruling terminating the procedure of public summons for exhortation under Article 198 of the Civil Procedure Law shall be signed by the judge and the clerk, and affixed with the seal of the People's Court."

16. Article 239 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where an interested person initiates a lawsuit with the People's Court in accordance with Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court may hear the case as an instrument dispute under the ordinary procedure."

17. The first paragraph of Article 256 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The other legal instruments enforced by the People's Court as referred to in the second paragraph of Article 201 of the Civil Procedure Law include arbitral awards and notarized documents of obligatory rights."

18. Article 257 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The suspension of enforcement as provided for in Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law shall be limited to the scope of property in respect of which a person not involved in the case raises an objection in accordance with that Article. Enforcement shall not be suspended in respect of other property of the person subject to enforcement. If the grounds for the objection are not established, the objection shall be notified for rejection."

19. The first paragraph of Article 265 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with the second paragraph of Article 206 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court at the next higher level above the entrusted People's Court shall, within five days after receiving the request from the entrusting People's Court to direct enforcement, issue a written instruction to the entrusted People's Court to enforce, and shall promptly inform the entrusting People's Court of this situation."

20. Article 267 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "An application for the resumption of enforcement of the original legal instrument shall be governed by the provisions on the time limit for applying for enforcement in Article 215 of the Civil Procedure Law. The time limit for applying for enforcement shall be suspended due to the conclusion of a settlement agreement during enforcement, and the time limit shall be calculated continuously from the last day of the performance period stipulated in the settlement agreement."

21. Article 268 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where the People's Court decides to defer enforcement in accordance with Article 208 of the Civil Procedure Law, if the security has a time limit, the period of deferred enforcement shall be consistent with the security period, but shall not exceed one year at most. If the person subject to enforcement or the guarantor transfers, conceals, sells, damages, or otherwise disposes of the secured property during the period of deferred enforcement, the People's Court may resume compulsory enforcement."

22. Article 269 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The enforcement security as referred to in Article 208 of the Civil Procedure Law may be provided by the person subject to enforcement by offering property to the People's Court as security, or may be provided by a third party as a guarantor. If property is offered as security, a letter of guaranty shall be submitted; if a third party provides security, a surety bond shall be submitted. The guarantor shall have the ability to perform on behalf of the debtor or to bear compensation liability on behalf of the debtor."

23. Article 271 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with Article 209 of the Civil Procedure Law, if, during enforcement, the legal person or other organization that is the person subject to enforcement is divided or merged, its rights and obligations shall be assumed by the legal person or other organization resulting from the change; if it is abolished, and there is a successor of rights and obligations under the relevant substantive law, that successor of rights and obligations may be ruled as the person subject to enforcement."

24. Article 275 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where, after the enforcement of other legal instruments enforced by the People's Court as provided by law, such legal instruments are lawfully revoked by the relevant authority, upon application by the party, the provisions of Article 210 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply."

25. Article 278 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with the second and third paragraphs of Article 213 of the Civil Procedure Law, after the People's Court rules to refuse enforcement of an arbitral award, the parties may conclude a new written arbitration agreement to apply for arbitration, or may initiate a lawsuit with the People's Court."

26. Article 279 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The enforcement notice referred to in the first paragraph of Article 216 of the Civil Procedure Law shall be issued by the People's Court within ten days after receiving the written application for enforcement. In addition to ordering the person subject to enforcement to perform the obligations specified in the legal instrument, the enforcement notice shall also notify him to bear the interest for delayed performance or the damages for delayed performance as provided for in Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law."

27. Article 282 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where the People's Court has, in the course of enforcement, sealed up or frozen the property of the person subject to enforcement in accordance with Articles 218 and 220 of the Civil Procedure Law, no unit, including any other People's Court, shall seal up, freeze, or thaw the same property again without authorization. Any violator shall be dealt with in accordance with Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law."

28. Article 283 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with Article 228 of the Civil Procedure Law, if a party fails to perform an act obligation specified in a legal instrument, and if such act obligation can only be performed by the person subject to enforcement, the People's Court may deal with the matter in accordance with Article 102(1)(6) of the Civil Procedure Law."

30. Article 288 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "If property that should be seized according to law is discovered during a search, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the second paragraph of Article 221 and Article 223 of the Civil Procedure Law."

31. Article 292 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "If, in the course of enforcement, the People's Court needs to handle the transfer of property right certificates such as real estate certificates, land certificates, forest ownership certificates, patent certificates, trademark certificates, vehicle licenses, etc., it may handle the matter in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law."

32. Article 294 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "The double payment of interest on debts during the period of delayed performance as provided for in Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law means doubling the interest on debts calculated at the highest loan interest rate of the bank for the same period."

33. Article 296 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where a creditor requests the People's Court to continue enforcement in accordance with Article 230 of the Civil Procedure Law, such request shall not be subject to the time limit specified in Article 215 of the Civil Procedure Law."

34. Article 305 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with Articles 34 and 244 of the Civil Procedure Law, for cases falling under the exclusive jurisdiction of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, the parties shall not, by written agreement, choose the jurisdiction of a court of another country, unless the agreement chooses arbitration."

35. Article 307 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "For a defendant not residing within the territory of China, where the complaint or summons is served by means of announcement and the defendant fails to appear after the expiration of the announcement period, after the People's Court renders a default judgment, the judgment document shall still be served by announcement in accordance with Article 245(7) of the Civil Procedure Law. If, from the day following the expiration of six months after the service of the judgment document by announcement, the party fails to appeal within the thirty-day appeal period, the judgment of first instance shall take legal effect."

36. Article 313 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "Where an arbitral award made by a foreign-related arbitration institution of China is not performed by one party, and the other party applies to the People's Court for enforcement, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of Chapter 27 of the Civil Procedure Law."

37. Article 315 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "When the People's Court compulsorily enforces an arbitral award made by a foreign-related arbitration institution, if the person subject to enforcement pleads that there exists any of the circumstances specified in the first paragraph of Article 258 of the Civil Procedure Law, after providing property as security, enforcement may be suspended. The People's Court shall examine the plea of the person subject to enforcement and, based on the result of the examination, shall rule to refuse enforcement or reject the plea."

38. Article 317 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1992] No. 22) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with Article 256 of the Civil Procedure Law, where a foreign-related arbitration institution of China submits a party's application for property preservation to the People's Court for a ruling, the People's Court may examine the application and decide whether to grant preservation. If it rules to take preservation measures, it shall order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, it shall rule to reject the application."

39. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether the People's Court May Lawfully Take Compulsory Measures against the Deposits of Commercial Banks with the People's Bank of China (Fa Fu [1995] No. 4) is adjusted as follows: "A specialized bank is a commercial bank established according to law and is an enterprise legal person that bears civil liability with all its legal person property. In accordance with Article 218 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, if a specialized bank that is a person subject to enforcement fails to voluntarily perform the obligations specified in an effective legal instrument in accordance with the enforcement notice, the People's Court has the authority to inquire into, freeze, and transfer the deposits of such specialized bank with the People's Bank of China; the relevant People's Bank of China must promptly handle the matter in accordance with the assistance enforcement notice (with the effective legal instrument attached); if it refuses to assist in enforcement, legal liability shall be pursued according to law."

40. Article 2 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the People's Court's Handling of Matters Related to Foreign-Related Arbitration and Foreign Arbitration (Fa Fa [1995] No. 18) is adjusted as follows: "Where a party applies to the People's Court for enforcement of an award of a foreign-related arbitration institution of China, or applies to the People's Court for recognition and enforcement of an award of a foreign arbitration institution, if the People's Court considers that the award of the foreign-related arbitration institution of China falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 258 of the Civil Procedure Law, or that the foreign arbitral award sought to be recognized and enforced does not comply with the provisions of an international convention to which China is a party or does not meet the principle of reciprocity, before ruling to refuse enforcement or to refuse recognition and enforcement, the People's Court must submit the matter to the Higher People's Court of the jurisdiction for review; if the Higher People's Court agrees to refuse enforcement or refuse recognition and enforcement, it shall report its review opinion to the Supreme People's Court. Only after obtaining a reply from the Supreme People's Court may the ruling to refuse enforcement or to refuse recognition and enforcement be made."

41. Paragraph 2 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Earnestly Implementing the Arbitration Law and Enforcing Arbitral Awards According to Law (Fa Fa [1995] No. 21) is adjusted as follows: "Pursuant to the requirements of the Notice of the General Office of the State Council on Further Improving the Work of Reorganizing Arbitration Institutions (Guo Ban Fa [1995] No. 38), cases accepted by existing arbitration institutions before their termination according to law shall have arbitral awards made within six months from the date of termination of such arbitration institutions according to law. Therefore, if an arbitration institution submits a party's application for property preservation to a People's Court during this period, the People's Court shall render a ruling in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, either accepting the application or rejecting it; if a written award or mediation statement made by an arbitration institution in accordance with the arbitration procedure during this period is not performed by one party, and the other party applies to a People's Court for enforcement in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court to which the application is made shall enforce it. However, if the respondent provides evidence that the award falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 213, Paragraph 2 or Article 258, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, or if a party provides evidence that the award falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 258, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law or Article 58 of the Arbitration Law, the court shall respectively render a ruling of non-enforcement or revocation of the award. If one party applies for enforcement and the other party applies for revocation of the award, the People's Court shall rule to suspend enforcement."

42. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether the People's Court Has the Right to Inquire, Freeze and Deduct Postal Savings Deposits According to Law (Fa Fu [1996] No. 1) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with the provisions of Article 65 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court has the right to investigate and collect evidence from relevant entities, including postal enterprises, and such entities shall not refuse.
"The phrase 'other entities with savings business' in Articles 103, 218 and 219 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China includes postal enterprises handling postal savings business. For the purposes of property preservation, advance execution, or enforcement of legally effective legal instruments, the People's Court has the right to inquire, freeze, and deduct postal savings deposits handled by postal enterprises; the relevant postal enterprises shall assist the People's Court in inquiring, freezing, and deducting according to law."

43. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue That the People's Court Shall Not Accept a Retrial Application Filed by a Party Dissatisfied with the Ruling of Non-Enforcement of an Arbitral Award (Fa Fu [1996] No. 8) is adjusted as follows: "Pursuant to the provisions of Article 213 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, if a People's Court legally rules to refuse enforcement of an arbitral award, and a party dissatisfied with the ruling applies for retrial, there is no legal basis, and the People's Court shall not accept the application."

44. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether the Tax Authority Has the Obligation to Assist the People's Court in Directly Transferring Tax Refunds (Fa Fu [1996] No. 11) is adjusted as follows: "Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the State Administration of Taxation's Measures for the Administration of Export Tax Refunds (Exemptions), enterprise export tax refunds, after being examined and approved by the state tax authority, shall go through specific procedures to be refunded to the export enterprise through a bank (the state treasury). The state tax authority is only the examination and approval authority for enterprise export tax refunds and does not hold the refunded amounts. Therefore, the People's Court may not, in accordance with the provisions of Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, require the tax authority to directly transfer the tax refunds due to the enforcement respondent. However, the People's Court may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, request the tax authority to provide information such as the enforcement respondent's tax refund account at the bank, the amount of the tax refund, and the timing of the refund, and may, based on the enforcement respondent's tax refund account provided by the tax authority, notify the relevant bank according to law to freeze or transfer the amount to be enforced."

45. Paragraph 2 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Fa [1997] No. 4) is adjusted as follows: "During arbitration proceedings, if a party applies for property preservation, for ordinary cases, the Primary People's Court at the place of domicile of the respondent or the place where the property is located shall render a ruling; for foreign-related arbitration cases, in accordance with the provisions of Article 256 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Intermediate People's Court at the place of domicile of the respondent or the place where the property is located shall render a ruling. The relevant People's Court shall carefully examine the application for property preservation submitted by the arbitration institution; if it conforms to the legal provisions, it shall promptly render a ruling on property preservation according to law; if it finds that the application does not conform to the legal provisions, it shall render a ruling rejecting the application according to law."

46. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Handle Cases Where the Borrower Fails to Repay the Loan Upon Expiry of an Enterprise Loan Contract (Fa Fu [1996] No. 5) is adjusted as follows: "An enterprise loan contract that violates relevant financial regulations is an invalid contract. After the contract term expires, if the borrower fails to repay the principal upon expiry and the parties file a lawsuit with the People's Court, the People's Court shall, in addition to rendering a judgment in accordance with the relevant provisions of Item 2 of Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Joint Venture Contracts (Fa (Jing) Fa [1990] No. 27), confiscate the interest accrued from the date of the repayment deadline agreed by the parties until the date specified in the court's judgment for the borrower to repay the principal. Such interest shall be calculated at the interest rate originally agreed upon by the lender and the borrower; if no interest rate was agreed upon, it shall be calculated at the bank lending rate for the corresponding period. If the borrower fails to repay the principal within the time limit specified in the judgment, it shall pay double the interest for the period of delayed performance in accordance with the provisions of Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China."

47. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Request for Instructions from the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court Regarding the Non-Enforcement of the Arbitral Award in the Dispute over a Performance Contract between American Production Company and Tom Hullett Company v. China Women's Travel Service (Ta [1997] No. 35) is adjusted as follows: "On August 28, 1992, American Production Company and Tom Hullett Company signed a 'Contract and Performance Agreement' for hiring American actors to perform in China. Clause 2(B) of the 'Contract and Performance Agreement' expressly stipulates: 'The actors shall do their utmost to comply with China's rules, regulations and policies and satisfactorily achieve the entertainment effect of the performances.' On September 9 of the same year, the two companies signed a 'Contract Appendix.' Clause 7(2) of the 'Contract Appendix' stipulates: 'China has the right to review and approve the details of the actors' performances.' Based on the above contract and agreement, the two U.S. companies signed a 'Contract and Agreement' with China Women's Travel Service on December 23, 1992, for a performance tour in China. It was agreed that the American Southern Band would perform 20 to 23 shows in China from January 25, 1993, to February 28, 1993. However, during the performances, the U.S. actors violated the contract agreement by not performing according to the content approved by the Ministry of Culture of China; they performed 'heavy metal songs' unsuitable for China's national conditions, which violated the social public interest of China, caused a very bad influence, and were ordered by the Ministry of Culture to stop performing. Thus, the cessation of performances and the reduction in performance revenue were caused by the serious breach of contract by the performing party. The Arbitral Award (94) Mao Zhong Zi No. 0015 of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission, which ignored the above basic facts, is completely erroneous. If the People's Court enforces this award, it would harm the social public interests of China. In accordance with the provisions of Article 258, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court agrees with your court's opinion of not enforcing this arbitral award."

48. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether Enforcement Measures May Be Taken Against the Certificated Treasury Bonds Held by the Enforcement Respondent in a Bank (Fa Shi [1998] No. 2) is adjusted as follows: "Certificated treasury bonds held by the enforcement respondent in a bank are marketable securities deposited with the bank for management, which bear principal and interest upon maturity, and are similar in nature to fixed-term savings deposits in a bank, constituting property of the enforcement respondent. In accordance with the spirit of Article 218 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court has the right to freeze and transfer the certificated treasury bonds held by the enforcement respondent in a bank. The relevant bank shall transfer the principal and interest to the enforcement applicant in accordance with the People's Court's notice of assistance in enforcement."

49. Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "Where a review is conducted on whether an arbitral award has grounds for refusal of enforcement under Article 213 or Article 258 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall be conducted by a collegial panel."

50. Article 24 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "After a People's Court decides to accept a case for enforcement, it shall, within three days, issue an enforcement notice to the enforcement respondent, ordering it to perform the obligations determined in the legally effective legal instrument within the specified time limit, and bear the interest on the debt for the delayed performance or the late performance fee as provided in Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law."

51. Article 30 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "If the enforcement respondent refuses to provide evidence materials concerning its property status as required by the People's Court, the People's Court may conduct a search in accordance with the provisions of Article 224 of the Civil Procedure Law."

52. Article 59 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "After the property of the enforcement respondent has been auctioned, sold, or ruled to be transferred in lieu of debt payment, if it needs to be delivered from the current possessor to the buyer or the enforcement applicant, the provisions of Articles 225 and 226 of the Civil Procedure Law and Articles 57 and 58 of these Provisions shall apply."

53. Paragraph 1 of Article 71 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "With respect to objections raised by a person not involved in the case, the enforcement court shall conduct a review in accordance with the provisions of Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law."

54. Article 83 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "Where a ruling is made to change or add an enforcement subject in accordance with Article 209 of the Civil Procedure Law, Articles 271 to 274 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law, and these Provisions, it shall be handled by the enforcement organ of the enforcement court."

56. Article 105 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "During enforcement, if the enforcement respondent is declared bankrupt by a ruling of the People's Court, the enforcement court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Item 6 of Article 233 of the Civil Procedure Law, issue a ruling to conclude the enforcement."

57. Article 109 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (Fa Shi [1998] No. 15) is adjusted as follows: "During or after enforcement, if the legal instrument upon which enforcement is based is revoked or modified by the People's Court or other relevant authority, the original enforcement organ shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 210 of the Civil Procedure Law, upon application of a party or ex officio, issue a ruling for the reversal of enforcement in accordance with the new legally effective legal instrument, ordering the original enforcement applicant to return the property and its fruits already obtained. If the original enforcement applicant refuses to return them, compulsory enforcement shall be carried out."

58. Paragraph 1 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Matters Concerning the Revocation of Foreign-Related Arbitral Awards by the People's Courts (Fa [1998] No. 40) is adjusted as follows: "Where a party applies to a People's Court for revocation of a foreign-related arbitral award of China in accordance with the Arbitration Law, if the People's Court, after review, finds that the foreign-related arbitral award falls under any of the circumstances provided in Article 258, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall, before ruling to revoke the award or notifying the arbitration tribunal to re-arbitrate, submit it to the Higher People's Court of the jurisdiction for review. If the Higher People's Court agrees to revoke the award or notify the arbitration tribunal to re-arbitrate, it shall submit its review opinions to the Supreme People's Court. Only after receiving the reply from the Supreme People's Court may it rule to revoke the award or notify the arbitration tribunal to re-arbitrate."

59. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether the People's Court Shall Accept a Protest Filed by the People's Procuratorate Against a Civil Mediation Statement (Fa Shi [1999] No. 4) is adjusted as follows: "Article 187 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China only provides that the People's Procuratorate may lodge a protest against a legally effective judgment or ruling of the People's Court, and does not provide that the People's Procuratorate may lodge a protest against a mediation statement. If the People's Procuratorate lodges a protest against a mediation statement, the People's Court shall not accept it."

61. Item 8 of Article 2 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Strictly Implementing the Time Limits for Case Adjudication (Fa Shi [2000] No. 29) is adjusted as follows: "In the adjudication of foreign-related civil cases, in accordance with the provisions of Article 248 of the Civil Procedure Law, the time limits for the adjudication of the above-mentioned cases shall not apply."

62. Article 33 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Negotiable Instruments (Fa Shi [2000] No. 32) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with the provisions of Article 196 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), the period for public summons for exhortation shall be sixty days from the date of publication of the announcement for domestic negotiable instruments, and may be appropriately extended for foreign-related negotiable instruments depending on the specific circumstances, but shall in no case exceed ninety days."

63. Article 34 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Disputes over Negotiable Instruments (Fa Shi [2000] No. 32) is adjusted as follows: "In accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 197 of the Civil Procedure Law, during the period of public summons for exhortation, if a negotiable instrument under public summons for exhortation is pledged or discounted, and the holder who accepts the instrument through such pledge or discount asserts rights under the instrument, the People's Court shall not support such assertion, except where the instrument is obtained after the expiry of the period of public summons for exhortation but before the People's Court renders a judgment of invalidating the instrument."

64. Paragraph 3 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues to Be Noted in the Trial and Enforcement of Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases (Fa [2000] No. 51) is adjusted as follows: "Strictly abide by the enforcement provisions for legally effective legal instruments in foreign-related civil and commercial cases, and effectively safeguard the judicial authority of the State. In the process of strengthening enforcement work, People's Courts at all levels shall recognize the importance of foreign-related enforcement work from the perspective of maintaining the judicial image of the State and the dignity of the legal system, further strengthen the enforcement of foreign-related cases, pay attention to enforcement methods, improve enforcement efficiency, and focus on enforcement effectiveness. The review and enforcement of foreign-related arbitral awards and foreign arbitral awards shall be handled strictly in accordance with the relevant international conventions, the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the provisions on foreign-related enforcement in the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), and the Notices: Fa (Jing) Fa [1987] No. 5, Fa Fa [1995] No. 18, Fa Shi [1998] No. 28, and Fa [1998] No. 40 of the Supreme People's Court. If a People's Court at any level intends to apply Article 258 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the provisions of relevant international conventions to refuse enforcement of a foreign-related arbitral award, revoke a foreign-related arbitral award, or refuse recognition and enforcement of an award made by a foreign arbitration institution, it shall, in accordance with the provisions, submit the matter level by level to the Supreme People's Court for review. No ruling shall be made before the Supreme People's Court replies."

65. Article 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Urging Procedure (Fa Shi [2001] No. 2) is adjusted as follows: "After receiving the written application of the creditor, if the People's Court finds that the application does not meet the requirements, it may notify the creditor to rectify within a specified time limit. The period for rectification shall not be counted in the time limit provided in Article 192 of the Civil Procedure Law."

67. Paragraph 3 of Article 83 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation (Fa Shi [2001] No. 33) is adjusted as follows: "For retrial civil cases accepted after these Provisions come into force, where the People's Court conducts trial in accordance with the provisions of Article 186 of the Civil Procedure Law, these Provisions shall apply."

68. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether Judicial Documents May Be Served on the Representative Office of a Foreign Company in China and Whether Service by Leaving at the Place May Apply (Fa Shi [2002] No. 15) is adjusted to: “Article 1 of the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters (hereinafter referred to as the Hague Service Convention) provides: ‘The present Convention shall apply in all cases, in civil or commercial matters, where there is occasion to transmit a judicial or extrajudicial document for service abroad.’ According to Article 245 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), a People's Court may serve litigation documents on a party who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China by the method specified in the international treaty concluded or jointly acceded to by the country where the party to be served is located and the People's Republic of China; when the party to be served has a representative office within the territory of the People's Republic of China, it shall no longer fall within the circumstance set forth in the Hague Service Convention of ‘where there is occasion to transmit a judicial or extrajudicial document for service abroad’. Therefore, the People's Court may serve litigation documents on the representative office established by the party to be served within the territory of the People's Republic of China in accordance with Article 245(5) of the Civil Procedure Law, without having to serve them abroad under the Hague Service Convention.
“According to Article 235 of the Civil Procedure Law, when a People's Court serves litigation documents on the representative office of a foreign company in China, service by leaving at the place may be applied.”

69. Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2003] No. 3) is adjusted to: “The jurisdiction over cases involving foreign-related maritime tort disputes and maritime transport contract disputes shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter 24 of the Civil Procedure Law; where Chapter 24 of the Civil Procedure Law has no provisions, the provisions of Article 6, paragraph 2, subparagraphs (1) and (2) of the Special Maritime Procedure Law and other relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply.”

70. Article 88 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2003] No. 3) is adjusted to: “The judgments, rulings, mediation statements and arbitration awards referred to in Article 115 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law mean the domestic judgments, rulings, mediation statements and arbitration awards of China. For foreign judgments, rulings, mediation statements and arbitration awards provided by a creditor, the procedures for examination as provided in Articles 266 and 267 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply.”

72. The second paragraph of Article 19 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Civil Mediation Work of People's Courts (Fa Shi [2004] No. 12) is adjusted to: “Where the party that fails to perform the mediation agreement has assumed the civil liability specified in the mediation statement in accordance with the preceding paragraph, and the other party subsequently demands it to assume the liability for delayed performance as provided in Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall not uphold such a demand.”

73. Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Civil Mediation Work of People's Courts (Fa Shi [2004] No. 12) is adjusted to: “Where a mediation statement provides for the delivery of a specific subject matter, the real rights and priority rights of a third party that already existed on that subject matter before the mediation agreement was reached shall not be affected. If the third party raises an objection to the subject matter of enforcement during the enforcement process, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law.”

74. The second paragraph of Article 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Sealing, Seizing and Freezing Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts (Fa Shi [2004] No. 15) is adjusted to: “The enforcement officers and the custodian shall sign the record. If any person specified in Article 221 of the Civil Procedure Law is present, the present person shall also sign the record.”

75. The Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Whether a People's Court Shall Accept a Party's Application for Recognition of a Certificate of Divorce Issued by a Court of Australia (Fa Shi [2005] No. 8) is adjusted to: “Where a party holds a certificate of divorce issued by a court of Australia and applies to a People's Court for recognition of its validity, the People's Court shall accept the case and shall conduct examination in accordance with Articles 265 and 266 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the relevant provisions of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Procedures for Chinese Citizens Applying for Recognition of Divorce Judgments of Foreign Courts, and shall lawfully render a ruling either recognizing or not recognizing the validity.”

76. The first paragraph of Article 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Enforcement of Mortgaged Premises by People's Courts (Fa Shi [2005] No. 14) is adjusted to: “After the expiry of the aforesaid grace period, if the person subject to enforcement still fails to vacate, the People's Court may render a ruling on compulsory vacation and enforce it in accordance with Article 226 of the Civil Procedure Law.”

77. Article 4 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Service of Judicial Documents in Foreign-Related Civil or Commercial Cases (Fa Shi [2006] No. 5) is adjusted to: “Unless the person to be served expressly states in the power of attorney that the litigation agent is not authorized to receive the relevant judicial documents on its behalf, the litigation agent appointed by it shall be the litigation agent authorized to accept service on its behalf as provided in Article 245(4) of the Civil Procedure Law, and the People's Court may serve the documents on such litigation agent.”

78. Article 9 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Service of Judicial Documents in Foreign-Related Civil or Commercial Cases (Fa Shi [2006] No. 5) is adjusted to: “Where a People's Court makes service by way of public announcement as provided in Article 245(7) of the Civil Procedure Law, the content of the announcement shall be published in newspapers distributed publicly both domestically and abroad.”

79. Article 17 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2006] No. 7) is adjusted to: “Where a party applies to set aside an arbitration award on grounds not provided in Article 58 of the Arbitration Law or Article 258 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall not uphold the application.”

80. The second paragraph of Article 27 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Arbitration Law of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2006] No. 7) is adjusted to: “Where a party raises an objection to the validity of the arbitration agreement during the arbitration proceedings, and after the arbitration award is made, claims to set aside the arbitration award or raises a defense of non-enforcement on such ground, if upon examination it complies with the provisions of Article 58 of the Arbitration Law or Articles 213 and 258 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall uphold it.”

81. The Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adding the Content of Informing the Parties of the Provisions of Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law in Civil Judgments (Fa [2007] No. 19) is adjusted in title to: “Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adding the Content of Informing the Parties of the Provisions of Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law in Civil Judgments,” and the content is adjusted to: “In accordance with the requirement of ‘implementing the system of informing the parties of their rights and obligations’ set forth in the Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Several Major Issues concerning Building a Socialist Harmonious Society, and for the purpose of enabling the prevailing party to obtain the litigation results in a timely manner and urging the losing party to fulfill obligations promptly, after study, it is decided to add the content of informing the parties of the provisions of Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law in civil judgments that contain an obligation to pay a sum of money. The specific expression in civil judgments is hereby notified as follows:
“1. Where a court of first instance judgment contains an obligation to pay a sum of money, it shall write a new line after all items of the judgment: ‘If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the party shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.’”
